en: The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Woman Dṛḍhā, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Narendrayaśas of North India during the Sui Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying in the city of Śrāvastī in the kingdom of Kośala at the Jetavana Grove.
At the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:
“Listen now with close attention!”
I shall explain this for you.
If there is a woman who wishes to give rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, she should first form this thought:

"All the deceit, crookedness, jealousy, greed, anger, hypocrisy, and all other evil deeds possessed by all women, by virtue of the causal conditions of giving rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, shall never arise again in future lives."
"For this reason, all women must certainly resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

When the Buddha had spoken these words, there was among the assembly a female lay follower named Sthira, who rose from her seat, adjusted her robes, joined her palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"

Now, for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, for the sake of bestowing peace and happiness upon all sentient beings, out of compassion for all beings in all worlds, and desiring to deliver all devas and humans, I have resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
“World-Honored One!

Regarding the beginningless cycle of birth and death in the past and the boundless flow of existence in the future, I feel no fear. Rather, for the sake of not severing the lineage of the Buddhas, for the sake of not severing the lineage of the Tathāgatas, and for the sake of not severing the lineage of omniscience, I have resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and cultivate the practices of a bodhisattva.”
“World-Honored One!

I now resolve to attain bodhicitta for the sake of bringing peace and security to all sentient beings; to act as a protector for those without protection, to act as a kinsman for those without kin, to act as a refuge for those without refuge, and to act as a dwelling for those without a home.”
At that time, the Elder Śāriputra, amidst the great assembly, had this thought:
"This sister Dṛḍhamatī has resolved her mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* for the sake of becoming a kinsman and friend to all sentient beings."
"Because of these causes and conditions for generating the resolve, there are śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas in the world.
Having thought this, he immediately addressed the girl, saying: "Sister!
"Because you have resolved to attain bodhicitta, you shall, in future ages, behold śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.
At that time, the girl Dṛḍhā said to Śāriputra:
"Since beginningless time, as I have wandered through saṃsāra, I have never before been able to resolve upon such bodhicitta; only now have I first attained it."
I have now attained great and wholesome benefit; I have well obtained this human body and well obtained this life span.

Having encountered spiritual friends in past lives, I never for a single thought-moment gave rise to the mind of a śrāvaka or pratyekabuddha. By virtue of these causes and conditions, I am now further able to give rise to the mind of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi for the sake of all sentient beings.
At that time, Śāriputra said to the girl Dṛḍhā:
"You have now well obtained benefit; you have well obtained a human body; you have well obtained a lifespan, that you are able to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
"As you have said, one should practice according to what has been taught.
Then the woman Dṛḍhā addressed the Venerable Śāriputra, saying:
"According to what I have said, I shall certainly practice it."
At that time, Śāriputra again asked the girl Dṛḍhamatī:
"How does a bodhisattva practice according to what has been taught?
The girl replied:

“Śāriputra! A bodhisattva does not delight in the stage of the śrāvaka, nor does he delight in the stage of the pratyekabuddha; he delights only in the body of the Tathāgata, the stage of the Tathāgata, and the stage of omniscience.”
"In this way, Venerable Śāriputra,
this is called a bodhisattva mahāsattva practicing according to what has been taught.
Furthermore, Venerable Śāriputra,"
When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva practices giving, they aspire to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and do not seek the stage of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha;

likewise, when practicing ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, or cultivating wisdom, they aspire to seek anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and do not seek the stage of a śrāvaka or a pratyekabuddha—this is called the bodhisattva-mahāsattva’s practice according to their words.
Śāriputra said to the woman Dṛḍhā:
"What benefit does one who practices according to the teaching obtain?
Please explain this to me."
When the woman Dṛḍhā heard these words, she said to Śāriputra,
"What is this 'benefit' that you wish to see? Śāriputra replied:
“Sister! I wish to see you give rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* for the benefit of others.
The woman said:
“The characteristics of that mind are like an illusion; how can one see any benefit in it?
Śāriputra said, “If you possess wisdom, you can exhaust suffering within this very body and attain arhatship.”
"If you cannot exhaust suffering with this body and attain arhatship, then your wisdom is indeed a great error.
The woman said, "Venerable Śāriputra!"

"If this body of mine were to attain arhatship, my wisdom would be inverted; because this body of mine does not take up arhatship, it shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in a future life. Therefore, you should know that my wisdom is not called inverted."
Then Śāriputra said to the girl Dṛḍhā,
“After how much time will you attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?
The girl replied:
"Venerable Śāriputra!
I am neither a Buddha nor an Arhat; I do not know when I shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
Just as Śāriputra has now attained the taintless wisdom of an arhat, you should know at what time I shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Śāriputra said: "I lack wisdom; I do not know when you shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The girl said:
"I vow that in birth after birth, I shall not rely on the wisdom of Śāriputra, which understands through others and gives rise to faith through others;
I vow to attain the wisdom of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, knowing it myself and awakening to it myself."
At that time, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra had this thought: "We abide in the stage of the Lesser Vehicle and have attained limited wisdom;
if we were to behold the wisdom of the Tathāgata, we would realize that the wisdom we have attained is most narrow and inferior, abiding as it does in a small stage and possessing small wisdom."
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra thought to himself:

"Although we have attained the fruit of arhatship, we are unable to extensively benefit sentient beings or perform the deeds of a great man (mahāpuruṣa). Only one who is a true great man and possesses the qualities of a great man can greatly benefit immeasurable sentient beings."
Just as the woman Dṛḍhā, for the sake of her own benefit and for the benefit of all sentient beings, gave rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Having formed this thought, he immediately asked the girl:
"What dharma is called 'anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi'?
The girl Dṛḍhā replied:
"Venerable Śāriputra! Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi is the most supreme and most excellent among all dharmas, with nothing surpassing it; this is called Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
Furthermore, Śāriputra,
regarding that which is called "anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi," I do not perceive any dharma as being anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Śāriputra said: "If you do not perceive any dharma named 'anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi,' how can you resolve upon bodhicitta with the desire to awaken to bodhi?"
The woman said,
"I have resolved to attain *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* so that sentient beings who practice deviant paths may be established in the right path."
Having heard these words, Śāriputra again asked the girl:
"When the Buddha attained anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, he did not perceive dharmas, he did not perceive the Path, and he did not perceive the fruit."
"What benefit do you see that you wish to awaken to bodhi?

Having heard this, the woman said to Śāriputra, "When I attain unexcelled, perfect, and complete awakening (anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi), all the disciples within my land—such as Śāriputra, Maudgalyāyana, and others—will witness this event; for this reason, I wish to awaken to unsurpassed bodhi."
Śāriputra said: "Sister! Within the dharma that cannot be apprehended, how can there be the thought of desire?"
The woman said: "So it is, so it is, Śāriputra!"
I wish to awaken to this dharma that cannot be apprehended.
Because a dharma that cannot be apprehended is neither attained nor unattained, for this reason I wish to awaken to *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Having awakened to *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, he turns the great wheel of Dharma;
when turning the wheel of Dharma, he causes all sentient beings throughout the trichiliocosm to hear and know it universally.
At that time, Śāriputra asked the sister Dṛḍhamati:
"How shall I know that when you attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in the future and turn the great wheel of Dharma, its sound will pervade the trichiliocosm?"
Then, the woman Dṛḍhā pressed the big toe of her right foot against the earth; immediately, the great trichiliocosm shook violently, yet the ground where Śāriputra sat remained unmoved.
At that time, Śāriputra had this thought:
"Now this woman has performed a great supernormal power, being able to cause the earth of this trichiliocosm to tremble everywhere; for what reason does the ground where I sit alone not move?"
"Is this the power of the Buddha, or is it my own power?
At that time, the World-Honored One, knowing the thought that had arisen in Śāriputra's mind, addressed Śāriputra, saying:

"In this very place, in the distant past, there were a thousand women all named Dṛḍhā who, at the spot where you now sit, gave rise to the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and manifested great supernormal powers to receive their prediction of enlightenment."

In a future age, when Maitreya appears, there shall likewise be one thousand women here, all named Dṛḍhā, who will resolve their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, manifest great supernormal powers, and receive the prediction of enlightenment; they shall become Buddhas named Jina-dṛḍha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Then the woman Dṛḍhā addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If the Buddha’s bodhi is not attained in the past, not attained in the present, and not attained in the future, why does the World-Honored One speak of the Buddhas of the three periods—past, present, and future?”
The Buddha said: “So it is, so it is!
A Buddha is not attained in the past, nor is he attained in the present, nor is he attained in the future.”

Therefore, when it is said that there are Buddhas of the past, future, and present, this is merely a conventional designation for the existence of the three periods of time; it does not mean that the Buddhas themselves undergo going, coming, or existing in the present.
At that time, the woman Dṛḍhā addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Because one awakens to and knows this Dharma for oneself through these causes and conditions, rather than hearing it from another, one must resolve to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.”
The Buddha said: “Excellent! Excellent!”
"One who can know in this way shall, in the future, attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The woman said:
"World-Honored One!"
Since there is no one who, having seen such dharmas as these, fails to attain bodhi, I shall therefore certainly and inevitably attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Buddha said:
"Sister! Will you teach and transform sentient beings in future ages?"
The woman said:
“World-Honored One!
There is no one who, having seen such a Dharma as this, would not bring about transformation. Therefore, I shall now certainly be able to transform sentient beings.”
The Buddha said,
"Will you become a great guide in a future age?
The woman replied:
“World-Honored One!
There is no one who, having seen such a Dharma as this, would not become a Great Guide; therefore, I shall certainly and surely attain the state of a Great Guide.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, stood before the Buddha holding *mandārava* flowers, and giving those flowers he held to the woman Dṛḍhā, he spoke these words:
"Take these flowers and scatter them over the Buddha.
Then, having received the flowers, the woman Dṛḍhā scattered them over the Buddha; by the Buddha's supernormal power, they remained suspended in the air.
At that time, the World-Honored One smiled. It is the natural law of all Buddhas:

whenever they smile, various rays of light—blue, yellow, red, white, purple, and the color of crystal—emanate from their mouths. These lights shine everywhere, reaching as far as the Brahma Heaven; they then return to the Buddha, circumambulate him three times, and re-enter through the crown of his head.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
The Buddhas do not manifest a smile without cause or for a minor reason."
"For what reason and by what cause do you smile thus?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Do you see this woman Dṛḍhā?"

This woman, having ended her life here, will cast off her female body and attain the male form; during the Constellation Eon (Nakṣatra-kalpa), she shall realize unexcelled, complete, and perfect enlightenment, and be known as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Samantadarśin.

When that Buddha Samantadarśin first preached the Dharma in his initial assembly, twenty hundred thousand million billion people exhausted all outflows, cast off their heavy burdens, and realized arhatship;
in his second preaching of the Dharma, fifteen hundred thousand million billion people realized arhatship;
in his third preaching of the Dharma, ten hundred thousand million billion people realized arhatship.
From that time forward, immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of beings attained the fruit of arhatship.

"In this way, Ānanda! Within the buddha-field of that Tathāgata Samantadarśin, there are no hells, hungry ghosts, or animals; all the sentient beings in that land have fully accomplished the ten paths of wholesome action. They do not engage in commerce, trade, or agriculture, for that buddha-land possesses immeasurable merits."

Therefore, if there are sons or daughters of good family who have resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, one should not give rise to a mind of contempt toward them; for only the Tathāgata clearly knows this matter, and it is not something that other śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and the like can understand.
"Therefore, Ānanda! Those who love and delight in me, and those who revere me, should not give rise to a mind of contempt toward bodhisattvas.

When the Buddha had finished teaching this Dharma, the Elder Ānanda, the Venerable Śāriputra, the firm upāsikā, and all the devas and humans, having heard the Buddha’s teaching, were filled with great joy.
The Sūtra on the Woman Dṛḍhā Spoken by the Buddha
